title: Third-Party / Vendor Risk Lifecycle
client_pain_point: Clients track vendors in spreadsheets outside the risk register; nobody notices a vendor's SOC 2 lapsed or a contract auto-renewed with no re-assessment.
proposed_requirement: Add vendor-specific fields to Entity (contract_end_date, criticality_tier, last_due_diligence_date) and a recurring due-diligence assessment trigger tied to contract_end_date.
why_it_matters: Vendor risk is the #1 source of third-party breaches; entities.type already has 'Vendor' but nothing distinguishes vendor lifecycle from an internal app.
related_gap: entities table has no contract/renewal fields; no scheduled reassessment exists anywhere in the app

title: Control-to-Framework Many-to-Many Mapping
client_pain_point: One MFA control satisfies SOX, ISO 27001, and a customer's vendor questionnaire simultaneously; auditors ask 'which frameworks does this control cover?' and today there's no answer.
proposed_requirement: Add a control_framework_map join table (control_id, framework_id, requirement_reference) so a single control can be reported against every framework it satisfies.
why_it_matters: Duplicate controls for equivalent framework requirements is the single biggest compliance-program inefficiency clients complain about.
related_gap: controls links to a single risk_id only; risk_frameworks exists but has no relationship to controls at all

title: Evidence Attachments on Assessments, Controls, and Issues
client_pain_point: Assessors are asked to 'show your work' — a screenshot, a policy PDF, an audit report — but today they can only type a text justification.
proposed_requirement: Add an evidence_attachments table (record_type, record_id, file_url, uploaded_by, uploaded_at) with upload endpoints wired into the assessment, control, and issue detail views.
why_it_matters: The original requirements doc explicitly calls out 'evidence/comments' for assessments; only a free-text justification field was ever built.
related_gap: assessment_responses.justification is the only evidence field in the entire schema; no file storage exists

title: Issue Root Cause & Corrective Action Plan (CAPA)
client_pain_point: Auditors close an issue, it reopens six months later because the fix addressed the symptom, not the cause — a classic finding in maturity assessments.
proposed_requirement: Add root_cause, corrective_action, effectiveness_check_date, and recurrence_count fields to Issue, plus a verification step before state can move to Closed.
why_it_matters: CAPA discipline is a named SOX/ISO control-maturity expectation; current issues table only tracks title/priority/state with no cause analysis.
related_gap: issues table has no root-cause or corrective-action fields; state can jump straight to Closed with no verification gate

title: Risk Appetite & Tolerance Thresholds
client_pain_point: A risk scoring 20/25 sits in the register with no signal that it breaches the board's stated risk appetite until someone eyeballs the heatmap.
proposed_requirement: Add a risk_appetite_thresholds table (category or department scoped, max_acceptable_score) and auto-flag/escalate risks whose inherent or residual score exceeds it.
why_it_matters: Risk appetite statements are a governance requirement in most frameworks (COSO ERM, ISO 31000); scoring today is descriptive, never evaluated against a limit.
related_gap: risks.inherent/residual scores are stored but never compared against any configured threshold

title: Segregation-of-Duties Approval Gate on Risk Acceptance
client_pain_point: An analyst self-assesses a risk as low and moves it straight to Monitor with no second set of eyes — auditors flag this as a SoD violation every time.
proposed_requirement: Require a second, different user's approval before a Risk can transition into 'Monitor' state when residual score exceeds the appetite threshold (depends on NR-005 and real auth).
why_it_matters: Segregation of duties on risk acceptance is one of the most commonly cited findings in internal audit reviews of GRC programs.
related_gap: risks.state transitions have no approval step and no enforcement that assigned_to != approver

title: Overdue-Item Notifications & Escalation
client_pain_point: A risk task's due_date passes and nothing happens — the owner finds out three weeks later when the auditor asks why it's still open.
proposed_requirement: A scheduled job that scans risk_tasks.due_date and risk_mitigations.target_date, and on breach both flags the record and emits a notification (email/Slack webhook) to assigned_to/owner.
why_it_matters: Timely remediation tracking is the difference between a GRC tool and a spreadsheet with better graphics; clients expect this as table stakes.
related_gap: due_date and target_date columns exist and are never checked against the current date anywhere in the app

title: Historical Risk Score Trending
client_pain_point: Leadership asks 'is our risk posture improving quarter over quarter?' and the only answer available is today's snapshot from /reports/risk-summary.
proposed_requirement: Snapshot risks_by_state, avg_inherent_score, and avg_residual_score into a risk_score_history table on a schedule, and add a trend endpoint/chart to the dashboard.
why_it_matters: Trend-over-time is the single most requested executive reporting feature in every GRC maturity conversation; a point-in-time snapshot can't show direction.
related_gap: risk-summary report is computed live from current rows with no historical persistence at all

title: Board-Ready Report Export (PDF)
client_pain_point: The compliance manager copies dashboard numbers into a PowerPoint by hand every month for the board pack.
proposed_requirement: Add a PDF export of the risk-summary report (totals, heatmap, top issues) generated server-side, downloadable from the dashboard.
why_it_matters: Board and audit-committee reporting is a recurring, high-visibility deliverable clients need to produce on a fixed cadence; JSON isn't presentable.
related_gap: reports/risk-summary only returns JSON; no export/rendering exists in either backend or frontend

title: Recurring / Scheduled Assessments
client_pain_point: Quarterly SOX control testing and annual vendor reviews are calendar-driven, but every assessment today has to be created manually one at a time.
proposed_requirement: Add a recurrence_rule (e.g. quarterly, annual) to AssessmentTemplate and a scheduler that auto-instantiates new RiskAssessment rows tied to the right risk/entity when a cycle comes due.
why_it_matters: Compliance calendars are inherently recurring; manual re-creation is exactly the kind of busywork a GRC tool is supposed to remove.
related_gap: assessment_templates has no recurrence concept; risk_assessments are only ever created one-off via the launcher form

title: Configurable Scoring Matrix per Methodology
client_pain_point: One business unit wants a 5x5 qualitative matrix, another wants a quantitative dollar-loss (FAIR-style) model — today every risk is forced into the same 1-5 likelihood x impact scale.
proposed_requirement: Let risk_methodologies.scoring_logic reference a structured scoring config (matrix size, band thresholds, or ALE formula) that risk-summary and dashboard calculations actually apply, instead of a free-text description.
why_it_matters: RiskMethodology.assessment_type already distinguishes Qualitative/Quantitative/Hybrid, but scoring_logic is never read by any code path — it's decorative.
related_gap: scoring_logic column exists on risk_methodologies but no code in backend/main.py or the frontend consumes it

title: Role-Based Access Control Enforcement
client_pain_point: Every user can currently edit or delete any risk, control, or issue through the API — a real compliance client would fail an access-review audit immediately.
proposed_requirement: Wire the existing users/roles tables into actual request authentication (replace the X-User header with a real session/token) and gate write endpoints by role (e.g. only Assessor role can submit assessments).
why_it_matters: CLAUDE.md already notes users/roles are 'standalone... for future auth' — this is the single largest gap between a demo and something a client could actually deploy.
related_gap: users/roles tables exist but nothing in main.py authenticates a request or checks role permissions before a write

title: Bulk Import / Export (CSV/Excel) for Risk Register
client_pain_point: Clients migrating off Excel or a legacy GRC tool have hundreds of existing risks and won't re-key them one at a time through a create form.
proposed_requirement: Add CSV import (validate + bulk-insert) and export endpoints for risks, controls, and entities, with column mapping and error reporting for bad rows.
why_it_matters: Onboarding is the first real interaction a new client has with the product; a register that can only be built one row at a time is a hard adoption blocker.
related_gap: every resource is create-one-at-a-time via the generic CRUD router; no bulk endpoints exist anywhere

title: Global Search & Cross-Entity Filtering
client_pain_point: A client with 500+ risks can't find 'the one about the Salesforce outage' without scrolling a single unpaginated table.
proposed_requirement: Add a global search bar (risk/control/issue name+description) and server-side filter/sort/pagination on the list endpoints, replacing full-table client-side rendering.
why_it_matters: The workspace dashboard renders the entire risks/controls/issues table client-side with no pagination — this won't scale past a demo dataset.
related_gap: GET /api/v1/risks (and siblings) has no search param and returns the full table; frontend renders all rows unpaginated

title: Business Unit / Multi-Tenant Segmentation
client_pain_point: A holding company wants each subsidiary to see only its own risk register while sharing common frameworks and control libraries at the parent level.
proposed_requirement: Add a business_unit/tenant scope to risks, controls, and issues (department_id already exists as a loose grouping) and filter list/report endpoints by the requesting user's assigned unit.
why_it_matters: Multi-entity organizations are a large share of the real GRC market; today's registry is a single flat global list with no isolation.
related_gap: department_id groups entities but risks/controls/issues aren't scoped or filterable by it in any endpoint or UI view

title: Continuous Control Monitoring via Real Integrations
client_pain_point: The current 'trigger-test' button randomly flips a control to Pass/Fail — real clients want controls tested by actually querying the system they monitor (e.g. an IdP for MFA enforcement, a cloud config API for encryption-at-rest).
proposed_requirement: Define a pluggable control-test interface (webhook or scheduled connector) so a control can be wired to a real external check instead of random.choice, with test history retained per control.
why_it_matters: Continuous Control Monitoring (CCM) is the direction the entire GRC market has moved toward; the current simulator is explicitly a placeholder (backend/main.py's random Pass/Fail).
related_gap: POST /api/v1/simulation/trigger-test uses random.choice(['Pass','Fail']) with no real signal source and no per-test history stored
